concepts.title: Observing Objects Around Us
concepts.definition: Look around a classroom and each object tells a story of material and make: a wooden bench, a steel tumbler, a cotton dress; observation asks what each thing is made of and why.
concepts.key_idea: Objects are made of materials, and the material decides the object's behaviour.
question_patterns: name five objects in your classroom and their materials
what is the difference between an object and a material
why is a bench made of wood and not glass
which objects around you are made of metal
can one object be made of many materials
group your classroom objects by material

solution_steps.explain: Note the colour, shape, feel or behaviour of the thing studied.
Write the observations in a table and group alike things together.
State the pattern your observations reveal.

concepts.title: Grouping Materials by Properties
concepts.definition: Materials are grouped by their properties: appearance, hardness, whether they dissolve in water, let light pass, or sink and float; sorting by property brings order to thousands of materials.
concepts.key_idea: Properties are the sorting keys: choose the property that answers your purpose and groups appear.
question_patterns: on which properties can materials be grouped
what are transparent and opaque materials
which materials dissolve in water
how do we test whether a material floats or sinks
group these materials as hard or soft
why is grouping of materials useful

solution_steps.explain: Note the colour, shape, feel or behaviour of the thing studied.
Write the observations in a table and group alike things together.
State the pattern your observations reveal.

concepts.title: Choosing Materials for a Purpose
concepts.definition: Why is a tumbler made of glass, steel or clay and not of cloth? Because holding water demands a material that is hard, opaque to leaks and safe; purpose selects the property, and the property selects the material.
concepts.key_idea: Function chooses material: every object around you is a property match for its job.
question_patterns: why is a tumbler not made of cloth
what properties should a water container have
which materials can make a transparent tumbler
why do we use metal for cooking vessels
can the same object be made of different materials
match three objects to the property that matters most

solution_steps.explain: Say what the concept means in one or two lines.
Recall the activity or example in the chapter that shows it.
Use the idea on a new example from your surroundings.

concepts.title: What Is Matter?
concepts.definition: Everything with mass that occupies space is matter, from stone and steel to water and air; materials are matter in different forms, and studying matter is studying the stuff of the world.
concepts.key_idea: Air, water and stone share one citizenship: all are matter, having mass and volume.
question_patterns: what is matter
is air matter even though we cannot see it
how can we show that air occupies space
do all materials have mass
name three states of matter around you
is light a form of matter why or why not
